candidates.exact_span: toxicity tests conducted on effluent discharges where no receiving water is available due to zero flow conditions.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether zero flow conditions excuse, modify, or still require toxicity monitoring affects applicable monitoring obligations (B). Whether zero flow is treated as a documented no-discharge state versus an unresolved evidence gap affects missing-evidence classification (C).

candidates.exact_span: If the receiving water is unsatisfactory as a result of instream toxicity (fails to fulfill the test acceptance criteria), the permittee may substitute synthetic dilution water for the receiving water in all subsequent tests provided the unacceptable receiving water test met the following stipulations:
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of what constitutes unsatisfactory receiving water or failure of test acceptance criteria determines whether substitution is permitted, changing which monitoring method was required (B) and whether subsequent test results constitute valid compliance evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: a synthetic dilution water control which fulfills the test acceptance requirements was run concurrently with the receiving water control;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this concurrent-control condition was satisfied affects whether synthetic dilution water substitution was authorized, changing monitoring-method obligations (B) and whether resulting test data are adequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: the test indicating receiving water toxicity has been carried out to completion,
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a receiving-water toxicity test was carried to completion is a precondition for authorized substitution; different readings change what monitoring was required and whether later results are valid evidence.

candidates.exact_span: the permittee includes all test results indicating receiving water toxicity with the full report and information required; and
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether all required toxicity test results and reporting were included affects satisfaction of substitution preconditions, changing monitoring obligations (B) and whether available records adequately document the testing basis (C).

candidates.exact_span: the synthetic dilution water shall have a pH, hardness, and alkalinity similar to that of the receiving water or closest downstream perennial water not adversely affected by the discharge, provided the magnitude of these parameters will not cause toxicity in the synthetic dilution water.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'similar,' which downstream water qualifies as 'not adversely affected,' and whether parameter magnitudes 'cause toxicity' affects whether authorized substitution occurred, changing monitoring-method requirements (B) and the validity of resulting test evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall collect two samples (flow-weighted composite if possible) from the outfall(s).
candidates.computation_change_reason: The mandatory two-sample obligation and the 'if possible' qualifier for flow-weighted composites affect what sampling was required (B) and whether reported results reflect adequate collection when composites were not flow-weighted (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall collect a second sample (composite samples if possible) for use during the 24-hour renewal of each dilution concentration for each test.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes a separate sample-collection obligation tied to each dilution-concentration renewal during toxicity testing; whether it applied affects which monitoring actions were required.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must collect the composite samples so that the maximum holding time for any effluent sample shall not exceed 36 hours for first use of the sample. The permittee must have initiated the toxicity test within 36 hours after the collection of the last portion of the first composite sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of holding-time and test-initiation timing determines whether sampling and testing met permit conditions (B) and whether reported toxicity results remain valid evidence or represent an inadequate/missing-evidence state (C).

candidates.exact_span: Samples shall be chilled to 6 degrees Centigrade during collection, shipping, and/or storage.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether chilling to 6 degrees C was required and satisfied affects monitoring-obligation compliance (B) and whether sample-handling deviations undermine the adequacy of reported results (C).

candidates.exact_span: A holding time up to 72 hrs is allowed upon notification to EPA and NMED of the need for additional holding time.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether notification occurred and whether additional holding time was needed determines if the 36-hour limit was excused, changing applicable monitoring conditions (B) and whether extended holding constitutes a documented exception versus inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must collect the composite samples such that the effluent samples are representative of the discharge duration, and of any periodic episode of chlorination, biocide usage or other potentially toxic substance discharged on an intermittent basis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sampling captured discharge duration and intermittent chlorination, biocide, or other toxic episodes affects which discharge events and parameters are subject to limit comparison (A), what representative sampling was required (B), and whether absent or partial data reflect conditional non-requirement, no-discharge, or missing required evidence (C).
